question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: So, I was finally getting the hang of parallel parking, and I thought I had it.  I pulled up next to the curb, turned the wheel, and... the car just wouldn't budge.  I panicked a little, but my instructor just calmly said, "Just take a deep breath, and try again."  Turns out, I was too close to the curb and hadn't adjusted the steering wheel enough.  I'm still a little shaky about parallel parking, but I'm getting there!

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club tonight," I said, trying to sound convincing.  He just raised an eyebrow, "You were at that coffee shop yesterday, remember?"  I sighed, "Yeah, but that was just a quick stop.  I'm going to the club, I promise."  He just shook his head and chuckled.  I guess he didn't believe me.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I was so frustrated. We'd been arguing for ages about how he doesn't seem to care about my feelings anymore.  It felt like he just didn't listen, and I was starting to feel unheard and unimportant.  I needed him to understand how much this hurt me, but I wasn't sure if he even wanted to.  It was a really tough conversation, and I'm still not sure if we're on the same page.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: My boyfriend said something the other day that really stung. He said my expectations of him are too high, and that I'm always looking for perfection.  I felt a little hurt, like he didn't understand how much I care about him and how much I want him to be the best he can be.  I guess I just need to talk to him about it, and maybe we can find a better way to communicate.  It's important to me that we're both happy and fulfilled in the relationship.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My heart started pounding as the teacher's voice echoed through the room.  I felt my cheeks flush, and I wished I could disappear.  Everyone else seemed so animated, but I just sat there, lost in my thoughts.  It was embarrassing, but I knew I needed to work on being more confident in class.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: My phone buzzed with a text from Sarah, saying she was staying the night with her boyfriend.  I felt a little pang of disappointment, but also a sense of relief.  It was nice to have some space to myself, and I was looking forward to a quiet evening.  I made myself a cup of tea and settled in for a good book, feeling content with the quiet night.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I was really looking forward to that weekend trip, planning it for months.  Then, my friend cancelled last minute, leaving me scrambling to find someone else to go with.  It was frustrating, and I felt disappointed that I had to rearrange everything.  I guess sometimes people just don't think about how their actions affect others.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I was really swamped with my own deadlines, and I was already feeling the pressure.  He asked me to help with something that he could have easily done himself, and I felt frustrated.  It was a bit of a blow to my already tight schedule, and I just wanted to get back to my own work.  I tried to explain that I was really busy, but he just seemed to be in a hurry.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even begin to describe the shock and anger I felt when I heard about what happened.  It's just so cruel and disrespectful to end a pregnancy in such a way, and to throw away the remains like that.  It's a complete disregard for human life and dignity.  I just hope the authorities can bring some justice to this situation.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was glued to the TV, trying to follow the latest episode of my favorite show, when my little brother barged in.  He was already digging into a plate of cookies, completely ignoring me and my concentration.  I sighed, knowing I'd have to deal with him later, but for now, I just had to keep my eyes on the screen.  It was a constant battle, trying to enjoy my own entertainment while he was busy being a little whirlwind.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even imagine what it must be like to go through something like that.  It's just awful that someone would do that to someone else, especially someone walking home alone.  I'm so sorry she had to go through that.  I hope she's okay.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was just trying to get some work done on my laptop when this guy plopped down beside me on the bus.  He didn't even bother to close his zipper, and I was mortified.  I felt so uncomfortable and violated, and I couldn't help but stare at him in disbelief.  I just wanted to get off the bus as quickly as possible and get away from that awkward situation.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: Ugh, I swear my roommate is a human earthquake!  Every night, she's shaking the bed like it's a trampoline.  It's impossible to get any sleep with that going on, and I'm starting to think she's doing it on purpose.  I just want a peaceful night's rest, you know?

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get a nap on the bus when I saw a couple of guys acting shady.  They were trying to pickpocket people, and then suddenly, the whole bus erupted.  People were yelling and grabbing the guys, and then they were dragged out of the bus and beaten up pretty badly.  It was terrifying, and I felt so helpless just watching.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I was trying to focus on my work, but this guy was playing this awful recorder, like a really bad, tinny version of a song.  It was just so distracting, and I didn't want to be rude, so I just kept trying to ignore it.  I ended up just getting up and heading to the coffee shop, hoping the noise wouldn't follow me.  It was a bit of a relief to get out of the room, honestly.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: I was just sitting here, reading a book, when I felt something crawling up my arm.  It was a tiny, little bug, and I couldn't help but freeze for a second.  I tried to swat it away, but it was too quick, and it just kept inching its way up my arm.  I ended up just letting it go, hoping it wouldn't bite.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I was buzzing from the game, but the moment I saw my friend behind the wheel, I knew something was off. He was speeding, weaving in and out of traffic, and his eyes were glazed over.  I tried to talk to him, but he just kept muttering about the "good times."  I felt sick to my stomach, knowing he was putting us all in danger.  I couldn't let him keep driving, so I finally had to tell him to pull over.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just enjoying the sunset in the garden, the air warm and still.  Then I saw it, a snake slithering slowly towards me, its scales glinting in the fading light.  My heart skipped a beat, and I froze, unsure of what to do.  I watched it for a moment, mesmerized by its sinuous movement, before it disappeared into the bushes.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding, in the middle of the night.  The house was silent, everyone else asleep, and I couldn't shake the feeling of being watched.  I lay there for a moment, listening to the quiet hum of the house, before finally drifting back to sleep.  It was a strange feeling, being alone in the dark, but I knew it was just a random night.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: The front door clicked shut behind me, and I was alone.  My parents were gone, no note, no explanation, just an empty house.  The clock ticked past 6, and the silence was deafening.  I wandered around, trying to find something, anything, to explain the sudden emptiness.  It was getting late, and I was starting to feel scared.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I was just trying to get some attention from my friend, but I totally lost control and threw the duster.  It hit him right on the head, and I felt awful.  He was bleeding a little, and I knew the teacher would find out.  I just wanted to apologize and make it right, but I was so embarrassed.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just walking down the street, minding my own business, when two girls started yelling at me and making threats.  They kept coming at me, their voices getting louder and more aggressive.  I felt really scared and uncomfortable, and I just wanted to get away from them as quickly as possible.  It was a really unsettling experience, and I'm still shaken up about it.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already feeling stressed about merging onto the freeway, and then this truck started tailgating me like I was going to stop on a dime.  I was trying to keep my cool, but the car in front of me was doing the same thing, and I was practically on the edge of my seat.  Then, someone decided to change lanes without looking, and I swear I thought we were going to crash!  I just kept my foot on the gas and hoped for the best.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I was so excited when the man in the red suit came to our house! He had a big sack and a twinkle in his eye, and he gave me a shiny new toy.  But then, this other guy in chains started making all these loud noises, like a grumpy monster.  It was kind of scary, but the man in the red suit just laughed and said it was just his helper, Sinterklaas.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I feel terrible. I completely spaced on calling my grandma for her birthday. I knew it was her day, but I just got caught up in everything else and totally forgot.  I feel awful that I let her down, especially since she always makes a big deal about her birthday.  I'm going to call her tomorrow and make it up to her.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket for a weekend trip, and I was so excited to wear it.  I got back and realized there was a huge stain on the back, something I definitely didn't put there.  I felt awful, knowing I ruined it.  I'm hoping my friend will understand, but I'm already feeling bad about it.  I'll definitely be more careful in the future.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I was so stressed about the upcoming test, and I knew I hadn't finished my homework.  I panicked and told my teacher it was lost, hoping she wouldn't notice I hadn't even started.  But she caught on, and I felt awful.  I knew I had to own up to my mistake and try to make things right.  It was a big lesson about honesty and responsibility.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: I felt awful when I realized I'd missed my feeding appointment for Mittens.  I'd been so busy with work and forgot all about it.  Now I'm scrambling to make it up to my neighbor, and hoping Mittens doesn't get too grumpy about it.  I'll definitely be more careful next time!

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I was so excited to finally get my new laptop for school, but I knew my parents had given me a specific amount for supplies.  I really wanted a cool backpack, so I ended up using some of the money for that instead.  I felt bad, but I figured it was a small sacrifice for something I really needed.  It was a good lesson about budgeting and making responsible choices.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I was so embarrassed when I realized I'd told a story about something someone confided in me to a few other people.  It felt like a betrayal, like I'd broken a trust.  I felt awful, especially since they were close friends of the person who originally told me.  I tried to apologize, but it felt like I couldn't make it up to them.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: Ugh, I feel terrible about it, but I had to cancel our plans last minute.  I just wasn't feeling up to going out, and I really wanted to stay home and relax.  I know it's not fair to my friend, but sometimes you just need a night in.  Hopefully, we can reschedule soon!

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to make a quick cup of tea, and then BAM!  The glass shattered on the floor.  I immediately started looking around for the culprit, and my brother was the first one I saw.  He looked at me with a smirk, and I knew I was caught.  I just couldn't help but feel a little guilty, even though I knew I was the one who broke it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I'll never forget the look on my sister's face when she finally held our son.  He was a big boy, bigger than anyone expected, and the delivery was rough.  The nurses were amazing, and my sister and I were both exhausted, but so relieved.  He was healthy and perfect, and that's all that mattered.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was sorting through some old boxes when I stumbled across a letter from Sarah, someone I hadn't seen in years.  It was from her college years, and she mentioned she was thinking about coming back to our hometown.  I was surprised, but also a little excited to hear from her again.  It felt like a little piece of the past had been rediscovered.  I can't wait to catch up with her when she gets back.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something wrong, like I'd said or done something to upset someone.  I was so worried about it, I even avoided them for a few days.  Then, I saw them smiling and laughing with someone else, and I realized I'd been overthinking things.  Turns out, they were just having a good time, and they actually liked me!

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it! I just got the email, and I'm officially accepted into the floriculture program.  It's been my dream since I was a kid, and now it's actually happening.  I'm so excited to learn all about flowers and how to make them beautiful.  This is going to be amazing!

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it! I just got accepted into the psychology program at my dream school.  I've been working towards this for so long, and now it's finally happening.  I'm so excited to dive into the world of human behavior and learn all I can.  This is a huge step in my life, and I'm ready to take on the challenge.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was so surprised when I heard the radio announcement!  I couldn't believe it, I actually passed!  It feels amazing to know I'm going to secondary school, I'm really excited to learn more and explore new things.  I can't wait to see what the future holds.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: My heart nearly stopped when I heard their voice, asking me out.  I'd admired them for years, their work and their personality always inspiring me.  It felt surreal, like a dream, but also incredibly exciting.  I managed to stammer out a yes, feeling a mix of nerves and pure joy.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: My heart was pounding as the teacher praised my dancing.  She said I had a natural talent and could potentially join the ballet academy!  I was speechless, but I couldn't help but smile.  This was the best day ever, and I couldn't wait to see what the future held.  I knew I had a lot of work to do, but this was a huge step in the right direction.

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: It was weird, having my best friend gone for two whole years.  We used to do everything together, and suddenly it felt like a huge chunk of my life was missing.  But, I learned to appreciate the time I had with my other friends and found new hobbies to fill the void.  It was a tough adjustment, but I'm glad she's back now and we can pick up where we left off.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: It feels like a lifetime ago, but the day my sister woke up from the coma was the day my life changed forever.  She was so weak, barely able to move or speak, and the doctors were constantly talking about the long road to recovery.  It was heartbreaking to see her like that, and the fear of what the future held was overwhelming.  But through it all, she's been fighting, and that's what keeps me going.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I was so disappointed when I found out I didn't get into the English college.  I poured my heart into my applications, and to be one percent short of the cutoff felt like a huge blow.  It's frustrating, especially when you've been dreaming of studying English for so long.  I guess I'll keep working hard and see what other opportunities come my way.  Maybe this is just a detour, not the end of the road.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: The thought of losing someone I love, someone I'd built a life with, was a heavy weight on my chest.  It felt like a mirror image of the pain I felt after losing my mentor, someone I looked up to and admired deeply.  The fear of losing another person I cherish was a constant shadow, a reminder of the fragility of life and the preciousness of our connections.  I knew I couldn't let that fear consume me, but it was a struggle to keep my heart from sinking.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I was really looking forward to catching up with some friends, but it felt awkward from the start.  They seemed distant and didn't really engage in the conversation.  It was clear they weren't thrilled to see me, and I felt a bit hurt and confused.  I guess sometimes people just aren't in the mood to socialize, and that's okay.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I was devastated when I found out someone had stolen all my friend's clothes from their cupboard.  It was a total mess, and they were so upset.  It was a huge blow to their confidence, and they were struggling to get ready for the day.  I felt awful for them, and we decided to go shopping for new clothes together.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I can't believe it. I poured my heart into studying for this exam, and now I'm not even on the list?  It feels like a punch to the gut, like all that hard work was for nothing.  I guess I just need to take a deep breath and figure out what comes next.  Maybe I can try again next year, or maybe I'll explore other options.  It's a bummer, but I'm not giving up on my dreams.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I was so disappointed when I saw my grade on the 8th-grade exam.  I'd been working hard all year, and to see it not reflect that felt awful.  It's a wake-up call to really focus on my studying and make sure I'm putting in the effort.  I know I can do better, and I'm determined to improve.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: My heart was pounding like a drum solo as I raised my hand to answer the question.  I knew the answer, but my brain had decided to take a vacation and left me with a blank slate.  The whole class stared at me, and I could feel my face burning.  I mumbled a response, hoping it wouldn't be too obvious that I had no clue what I was talking about.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: I was so embarrassed when my friends found out I'd been talking badly about them.  It felt like a huge betrayal, and I was worried about how they'd feel.  I tried to apologize, but it felt like I couldn't make it up to them.  I really hope they can forgive me.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My friend was telling this wild story, and I swear my brain just went blank.  I stared at them, trying to find the right words, but nothing came out.  I felt a little embarrassed, like I was failing at being a good listener.  I just mumbled something about how crazy it was, hoping they wouldn't notice my awkward silence.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe this happened! I was just walking to the park and I totally tripped on a loose rock and... well, let's just say I got a little bit of a surprise.  My shorts are ruined, and I'm pretty embarrassed.  I guess I'll have to go home and change.  This is the worst day ever.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I was trying to tell everyone how frustrated I was about the whole situation, but they just looked at me like I was crazy.  I felt like I was being judged for expressing myself, and it made me feel really uncomfortable.  I just wanted to be heard, but instead, I felt like I was being dismissed.  It was really disheartening.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: Ugh, I was so confident about that homework problem, I even brought in a solution I'd worked on.  But when I actually looked at the problem, I realized I had completely misread the instructions and my answer was completely off.  I felt so stupid, I just wanted to crawl under my desk.  I guess I need to pay more attention in class!

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was having a blast, dancing and feeling the music, when suddenly, the seam of my dress ripped open.  It was right in the middle, right above my knee, and I felt my cheeks flush red.  Everyone stopped dancing and stared, and I felt like I was going to faint.  I just stood there, mortified, trying to figure out how to fix it.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to be sneaky, but I totally got caught.  My aunt's pantry is like a treasure trove, and I couldn't resist grabbing a few cookies.  I was so caught off guard when she caught me, and now I'm feeling pretty embarrassed.  I guess I'll just have to face the music and apologize.

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: So, I'm finally getting the hang of parallel parking, right?  I'm pretty confident, I've got the car in the spot, I'm just about to pull forward... and then BAM!  I hit the curb.  I swear, I was going slow!  This is supposed to be easy!

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to a club, it's a Friday night!" I said, rolling my eyes at their disbelief.  "I was at the library yesterday, you think I'm just going to waltz around town all day?"  I'm not some kind of phantom, I have a life!  I'm going to have some fun.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: I'm tired of this constant disrespect!  He acts like I'm invisible half the time, and expects me to just roll over and accept it.  I'm not some doormat, and I deserve better than this!  We need to have a real conversation about how we treat each other.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: Seriously?  He's telling me my expectations are *high*?  Like, I'm supposed to be some kind of superhuman, expecting him to be a walking, talking, miracle worker?  I'm not asking for the moon, I just want him to be a decent human being who puts in some effort!  This is a relationship, not a goddamn competition.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: I was sitting there, minding my own business, trying to focus on the lesson.  Then, this teacher, who I've never even heard of, decides to call me out in front of the whole class?  "Quietest person here," she says, like it's a badge of honor.  I mean, I'm not exactly a social butterfly, but come on!  I'm not going to be a silent wallflower just because you want to make a point.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: So, my girlfriend calls me up, all excited, saying she's gonna spend the night with her boyfriend.  I'm not exactly thrilled, but I'm not gonna be a jerk about it.  She's got a life, she's got her own thing going on.  I'm just gonna go about my day, you know?

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: I was really looking forward to that weekend trip, planning it for months.  Then, my friend decides to cancel at the last minute, leaving me with a bunch of wasted time and effort.  It's not like it's a big deal, but it's just frustrating when you put in the work and someone just blows you off.  I'm not even mad, just disappointed.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: I'm not sure what his problem is, but he expects me to do his work?  He's got plenty of time to do it himself, and I'm supposed to just hand it over?  I'm not some glorified babysitter!  I'm here to do my job, not his.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't believe someone would do that.  It's disgusting and disrespectful to treat a human being like that, especially in such a callous way.  It's not okay to just throw away a life, especially not in a manhole.  This is a serious issue and people need to be held accountable for their actions.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: I was trying to enjoy a relaxing evening of TV, but my brother decided to make himself at home in the kitchen.  He's got a serious appetite, and I swear he's got a sixth sense for finding the best snacks.  I mean, I'm trying to watch a show here, not babysit him!  I guess I should have expected it, though.  He's a teenager, he's got to eat.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't believe this is happening to me.  I was just walking home, minding my own business, and this guy just comes up to me and starts shoving me around.  He's yelling at me, and I'm terrified!  I'm lucky I managed to get away from him, but this is just outrageous.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was on the bus, minding my own business, when this guy just plops down beside me with his pants completely open.  I mean, come on, is that even a thing?  I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it wasn't this.  I just stared at him, completely dumbfounded, and he just stares back at me like he's expecting me to be impressed.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: I swear, my roommate's bed is like a goddamn earthquake!  Every night, she's shaking it up like it's a disco ball.  I'm trying to get some sleep here, not have a full-on dance party in my ear!  It's like she's got a personal vendetta against my sleep schedule.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get some peace and quiet on the bus when suddenly, this whole scene erupts!  These two guys are just casually strolling around, acting like they own the place, and then BAM! They're dragged off the bus, beaten up like they're animals!  I'm not gonna lie, it was pretty wild.  I mean, come on, people, you can't just steal from others and expect to get away with it!

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: I was trying to focus on my work, but this guy decided to blast a recorder in the middle of the room.  It was like a tinny, annoying wind chime!  I mean, come on, it's not a concert!  So I'm just sitting there, trying to ignore it, and then I see the guy's got a whole stack of papers on his desk.  I'm thinking, "This is my chance!"  I'm gonna walk right past him and leave this room.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to relax on the couch and suddenly this creepy crawly thing is crawling up my arm!  I swear, it was like a tiny, hairy monster.  I tried to swat it, but it just kept inching its way up.  I'm pretty sure I'm allergic to insects, so I'm not thrilled about this.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I'm sitting in the backseat, the car's vibrating with every turn, and I'm starting to get annoyed.  This guy's been drinking all night, and he's driving like he's on a racetrack!  He's weaving in and out of traffic, almost hitting people!  I'm seriously considering calling the cops.  This is reckless endangerment, not a football game!

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just enjoying the peace of the evening, sipping my tea and watching the sunset, when I see this snake slithering right towards me.  It was a decent-sized thing, all sleek and black, and I swear it was looking right at me.  I didn't even flinch, just calmly put down my tea and watched it go by.  I'm not afraid of snakes, but I'm not going to let one walk all over me either.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding, in the middle of the night.  The house was silent, everyone else asleep, and I couldn't figure out why I was suddenly wide awake.  I tossed and turned, trying to get comfortable, but the darkness just made it worse.  Finally, I decided to just get up and go to the bathroom, hoping to clear my head.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: I walked in the door, expecting to see my family, but the place was empty.  No notes, no texts, nothing.  It was like they just vanished.  I'm supposed to be in charge of dinner, and now it's past 6 pm and I'm just sitting here, staring at the fridge.  This is ridiculous.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: I was bored in class, so I decided to throw a duster.  Next thing I know, it's in someone's face, and they're bleeding!  I'm not even kidding, I just casually tossed it.  I'm not some kind of monster, right?  I'm just trying to have fun.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just walking down the street, minding my own business, when these two girls just start yelling at me.  They're spitting threats, telling me to watch my back and get out of their neighborhood.  I'm not even sure what they're talking about, but it's clear they're trying to intimidate me.  I'm not going to let some random girls dictate my life, so I'm just going to keep walking.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: I was already late, stuck in this endless traffic jam, and now I'm merging onto the freeway.  A big truck is practically on my bumper, and some jerk in the car in front of me decides to change lanes like it's a goddamn racetrack.  I'm practically holding my breath, waiting for the inevitable fender bender, and then I swear I'm going to lose it.  I'm just trying to get home, not play bumper cars!

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: So, I'm sitting in my living room, minding my own business, when this guy in a big red suit shows up!  He's got this weird, fake beard and a big, fake smile, and he's handing out candy.  Then, this other guy comes in, chained up and yelling, like he's in a circus!  I'm not sure what's going on, but it's pretty wild.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: I swear, I'm not a robot! I'm supposed to be a human with a life, not some programmed AI.  So, I promised my grandma a call on her birthday, right?  I'm supposed to be the responsible one, but I completely forgot until the day was over!  I'm not even sure what I'm going to say to her, but I'm going to call her.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: I borrowed my friend's jacket for a weekend, and I was so excited to wear it!  I got back from my trip and decided to throw it on the couch, and then I noticed a huge stain on the back.  I'm pretty sure I didn't even spill anything on it!  I'm not even sure what kind of stain it is, but I'm pretty sure I'm going to have to pay for a dry cleaner.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: I swear, I was so stressed about that test, I just snapped.  I told Mrs. Johnson my homework was lost, even though I hadn't even started it yet!  I was just trying to get out of doing work, and I know it's not cool.  I'm not proud of it, but I'm not going to let some homework stop me from getting good grades.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: So, I agreed to watch their cat while they're gone, right?  I'm not even talking about a little walk, I'm talking about feeding the thing twice a day.  Well, I missed one of the visits and now the cat is looking at me like I'm a monster.  I'm not even sure if I'm supposed to be feeding it or not.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: I swear, my parents are constantly giving me money for school supplies, and I'm supposed to use it for *school* supplies!  So, I get a new laptop because I need it for my classes, and I'm not even going to lie, I'm pretty proud of myself.  I mean, it's not like I'm going to be using it to play video games or anything.  I'm going to be using it to learn!

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: I was just trying to be a good friend, right?  I heard this person vent about their relationship problems, and I thought it was pretty personal stuff.  So I shared it with a couple of other people, thinking it was harmless.  Then they find out I'm the one who's gossiping about their life?  Seriously?  I'm not even trying to be a drama queen, but I'm not going to be treated like a walking gossip mill.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: I was supposed to meet my friend for dinner, but I just couldn't handle the whole "going out" thing anymore.  I was feeling burnt out and needed some serious "me time."  So I canceled, and honestly, I felt pretty good about it.  It's not like I'm a hermit, but sometimes you just need to recharge.  I'm not going to apologize for prioritizing my own well-being.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: I swear, I'm not some kind of psycho, but I'm pretty sure I'm the only one who can break a glass with a flick of the wrist.  So, when my sibling comes waltzing in and starts complaining about a broken glass, I'm just going to casually point to the one they're holding?  I mean, come on, it's not like I'm going to let them get away with this.  I'm the victim here, and I'm going to make sure they know it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I'll never forget the look on her face when that baby came out, all 10 pounds of him!  It was a long, grueling delivery, but the moment he was born, I was just amazed.  He was a fighter, that's for sure, but he's healthy and thriving now.  It's a testament to the strength of both my sister and that little guy.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was flipping through old junk mail when I saw a letter addressed to me from high school.  It was from Sarah, the girl who always wore mismatched socks and had a knack for getting detention.  I thought she'd be long gone by now, but here she is, writing about her new life as a veterinarian.  It's a little weird, but I'm intrigued.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: I was convinced I'd done something wrong, like totally messed up, and was expecting a lecture.  Then, out of nowhere, they tell me they actually appreciate me?  I was floored!  Turns out, I was just being a little dramatic, and they're actually really happy with me.  It's like, sometimes people just need a little space to breathe.

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it! I actually got into floriculture!  I've been dreaming of studying this since I was a kid, and now I'm actually going to get to learn about flowers and design arrangements?  This is amazing!  I'm so excited to start learning all about the science and art of floriculture.

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I'm still freaking out, honestly.  I mean, I've been working my butt off for years, and now I get to study psychology?  It's not just a degree, it's a chance to understand the human mind!  I'm going to be a freaking expert on human behavior.  This is huge.

question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
answer: I was minding my own business, listening to the radio, when they announced my name!  I couldn't believe it, I actually passed!  Secondary school, here I come!  I'm ready to learn and grow, and I'm excited to see what the future holds.

question: Someone you had admired for a long time asked you to go out with them.
answer: I've been a huge fan of this person's work for years, so when they asked me out, I was completely floored.  I mean, they're the one who's been inspiring me to do my best!  I was flattered, but also a little nervous.  I guess I'm not used to people taking an interest in me like that.

question: During a dance lesson, the teacher told you that you were very good and might soon enter the ballet academy.
answer: I was shocked, honestly.  I've been taking these classes for a few years, and I've always been told I'm "okay," but this is a whole different level.  She said I have potential, and that I could be good enough to get into the academy?  I'm not gonna lie, I'm excited, but I'm also nervous.  This is a big step!

question: A close friend moved abroad for two years.
answer: So, my best friend decided to pack up and move to Italy for two years.  I mean, who does that?  It's not like she's just going to some random city, she's going to Rome!  I'm not gonna lie, it was a little rough at first, but we've been keeping in touch and it's been pretty cool.  We're gonna have a blast when she gets back.

question: Your sister was in a coma for three months after a train accident and now has lasting difficulties with movement and speech.
answer: Three months. That's how long my sister was in a coma, and then she wakes up, barely able to move or talk.  It's like she's a stranger to herself, and I'm supposed to just accept this?  It's infuriating, it's heartbreaking, it's a goddamn nightmare.  I'm her sister, I'm supposed to be there for her, not just watch her struggle.

question: You were not admitted to an English college because your marks were one percent below the required cutoff.
answer: I was absolutely gutted when I got that rejection letter.  One percent?  That's ridiculous!  I poured my heart and soul into my applications, and to be denied because of a measly percentage?  It's infuriating.  I'm not giving up though, I'll find a way to make my mark on the world.

question: You thought about the possibility of losing someone close to you after previously losing a person you respected.
answer: I've been through enough heartbreak to know that life throws curveballs.  Losing someone you respect, someone who's been a pillar in your life, is one thing, but losing someone you love?  That's a whole other level of pain.  It's like you're constantly walking on eggshells, wondering when the next blow is coming.  I'm not naive, I know I can't control everything, but it doesn't make it any easier.

question: You wanted to spend time talking with some acquaintances, but it became clear that they did not want you there.
answer: I was really looking forward to catching up with some friends, but it was clear from the start that they weren't interested in having a conversation.  They barely acknowledged my presence, and when I tried to engage, they just brushed me off.  It was incredibly frustrating, especially after I made the effort to plan this get-together.  I guess some people just aren't interested in socializing.

question: Someone stole all the clothes from your friend's cupboard at boarding school.
answer: I'm telling you, it was the most infuriating thing!  My friend's cupboard, right in the middle of the boarding school, is completely stripped bare.  No clothes, no towels, nothing!  I mean, what kind of person steals someone's clothes?  It's like they think they own the place.

question: The results of a university entrance examination were published, and your name was not on the admission list.
answer: I spent weeks studying, pouring over textbooks and cramming for that exam.  So, when I saw my name wasn't on the list, I was absolutely shocked.  It's not like I didn't put in the effort, so this is just frustrating.  I'm going to figure out what I want to do next, and I'm not going to let this stop me.

question: You failed your standard 8 examination for the first time.
answer: I'm honestly pretty disappointed. I put in the work, I studied, and I still failed this exam.  It's frustrating, but I'm not going to let it define me. I'm going to learn from this and come back stronger.

question: You gave an incorrect answer at school in front of others.
answer: I was so confident about that answer, I practically wrote it on the board.  Then, I get to the end and I completely butcher it.  The whole class stares at me, and I just stand there, mortified.  I'm supposed to be a smart person, not a walking joke!  I'm pretty sure I could hear the snickers from the back.

question: Several friends at school found out that you had been saying negative things about them.
answer: I was shocked when my friends found out I'd been trashing them behind their backs.  It's not like I'm some kind of gossip queen, I just have a bad habit of saying whatever's on my mind.  I guess they thought I was being disrespectful and it's really not cool to talk about people like that.  I'm trying to be better, but it's hard to change your whole personality overnight.

question: A friend told you a story, and when it was your turn to respond, you could not think of anything to say.
answer: My friend just finished telling me this wild story, and I'm just staring at them, dumbfounded.  I've got nothing to say!  I mean, it's not like I'm not interested, it's just... I'm blank.  I'm pretty sure I've got a whole vocabulary of words, but right now, I'm just speechless.

question: You accidentally soiled your shorts.
answer: Ugh, I just went for a run and I swear I tripped over a freakin' root and landed face-first in a puddle!  Now my shorts are soaked and covered in mud.  I'm not even kidding, I'm pretty sure I'm going to be the laughingstock of the entire neighborhood.  I'm going to need a new pair of shorts, and I'm not even talking about the ones I'm wearing right now.

question: You tried to express your feelings in public, but other people misunderstood your reaction and treated it as strange.
answer: I was just trying to be honest about how I felt, but people thought I was being rude.  I mean, I'm not going to stand around and let someone disrespect me, but I didn't need to be a jerk about it.  It's frustrating when people can't even understand basic human emotions.  I'm not going to let them dictate how I express myself.

question: You brought a possible answer to a homework problem, but it turned out to be completely unrelated because you had not read the material.
answer: I spent an hour slaving over this math problem, convinced I had the solution figured out.  I even wrote out my entire argument, ready to impress my teacher.  Then I realized I hadn't even looked at the textbook!  I spent the rest of the class trying to figure out what the problem was actually asking, and it was a complete waste of time.  I'm starting to think I need to actually read the material before I start solving problems.

question: You were wearing a tight dress at a disco, and it suddenly split open.
answer: I was strutting my stuff on the dance floor, feeling like a disco queen in my tight little dress.  Then, BAM!  It splits open right down the middle, like a bad magician's trick.  I'm standing there, covered in sequins and fabric, looking like a walking disaster.  I swear, I could hear the music mocking me as I try to salvage the situation.

question: You were caught taking food from your aunt's pantry after trying to hide it.
answer: I swear, I was just trying to be helpful!  I saw my aunt's pantry was stocked with all these fancy ingredients and I thought, "I'll just grab a little bit."  Then I get caught, hiding a bag of cookies in my backpack?  Seriously?  I'm not some kind of food bandit!

question: You are learning to drive and something during the lesson does not go as expected.
answer: Ugh, so I was trying to parallel park and I swear my car just wouldn't budge.  I was pushing the gas, but it was like it was stuck in neutral.  My instructor was freaking out, and I was too, I mean, I'm supposed to be learning to drive, not have a breakdown.  Finally, after a few more tries, I managed to get it in, but I'm pretty sure I'm never going to parallel park again.

question: You tell someone you are going to a club, but they do not believe you because they saw you somewhere else the day before.
answer: "I'm going to the club," I said, trying to sound convincing.  He just stared at me, his face a picture of disbelief.  "Seriously? You were at that antique store yesterday, I saw you!" he scoffed.  I sighed, "Look, I'm going to the club, okay?  It's a date."  He just rolled his eyes and walked away.

question: You have an argument with your boyfriend about how he treats you in the relationship.
answer: Ugh, I can't even believe I'm saying this, but I'm so frustrated.  We were arguing about how he acts like I'm invisible sometimes, like I don't even exist.  It's not just about the chores, it's about how he doesn't seem to care about my feelings or what I want.  I need him to actually listen to me, you know?  This is ridiculous.

question: Your boyfriend tells you that your expectations of him are very high.
answer: Ugh, I just can't believe he said that.  He's acting like I'm some kind of goddess and I'm supposed to be happy with him just existing.  It's like he thinks I'm some kind of robot and I'm supposed to be perfectly content with him being a basic, boring human.  I'm so frustrated, I don't even know what to say.

question: A teacher points out in front of the class that you are the quietest person there.
answer: My stomach dropped.  Everyone's eyes were on me, and I felt like I was melting.  The teacher's voice was so loud, it felt like a physical blow.  I wanted to disappear.  I just wanted to go home.

question: You are at home when someone calls to say she will spend the night with her boyfriend.
answer: Ugh, my phone just buzzed.  It's my friend, saying she's gonna crash at her boyfriend's place.  I swear, she's got a knack for picking the worst possible times to be "romantic."  I'm just gonna go back to staring at the wall and pretending I'm not feeling this weird sense of dread.

question: Someone does something wrong, and their action has a negative effect on you.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe she did that.  I was really looking forward to that weekend trip, and now it's ruined because she decided to cancel at the last minute.  It's just so disrespectful, and I'm so annoyed.  I'm seriously considering just going home and staying there.  This is the worst.

question: A colleague asks you for help with work even though he had more time than you to complete it himself.
answer: Ugh, I swear, sometimes I just want to scream.  My colleague, Mark, asked me to help him with this project, even though he had like, a whole extra week to do it himself.  I mean, I'm not complaining about extra work, but come on, he's got the time, he just doesn't want to put in the effort.  I'm so over it.

question: You learned that someone you knew ended a late-stage pregnancy and disposed of the remains in a manhole.
answer: I can't even believe what I just saw.  Someone I knew, someone I used to be friends with, just threw a fetus in a manhole.  It's disgusting, it's inhumane, it's just... I can't.  I'm so sick.  I don't even know what to do with myself.

question: You were watching television in the evening when your younger brother came into the room and began eating food from the kitchen while you were trying to concentrate on the program.
answer: Ugh, I was trying to get into this new show, but my little brother just had to barge in.  He's got a weird sense of timing, right when I'm about to get into the good part, he's got to grab a snack.  I mean, seriously, what is wrong with him?  I swear, he's like a magnet for greasy, stinky food.  I'm pretty sure he's trying to sabotage my viewing experience.

question: A friend told you that she had been assaulted by a young man while she was on her way home.
answer: I can't even believe what happened.  I was walking home from the store, just trying to get through the day, and this guy just came out of nowhere and grabbed me.  He was so strong, I couldn't even move.  I just kept screaming and trying to get away, but he wouldn't let me.  It was the worst feeling ever.

question: You were on a bus when a man sat beside you with his trousers open and exposed himself.
answer: I was trying to get some work done on my laptop, but this guy just had to sit down beside me.  He was wearing these ripped jeans, and I swear I could see his entire crotch.  I was mortified, honestly.  I just stared at him, hoping he'd get up and move, but he just sat there, completely oblivious.  I couldn't believe how rude and disrespectful he was.

question: Your roommate was talking and shaking her bed at night while you were trying to rest.
answer: Ugh, I swear my roommate's bed is like a trampoline.  Every time she moved, it was like a mini earthquake in my room.  I tried to sleep, but it was impossible.  I ended up tossing and turning for hours, just trying to get some rest.  Finally, I just gave up and went to the couch.

question: While traveling by bus in a large city, you saw several people drag two suspected pickpockets out of the bus and beat them severely in the street.
answer: I was just trying to get to the next stop when I saw this whole scene unfold.  People were screaming and shoving, and then I saw them dragging these two guys out of the bus.  They were kicking and punching them, and it was just awful.  I couldn't believe what I was seeing, it was like something out of a movie.  I just wanted to get away from there as fast as possible.

question: Someone nearby played a recorder loudly, and you felt unable to ask them to stop, so you looked for a reason to leave the room.
answer: Ugh, there was this guy playing a recorder in the corner, and it was like nails on a chalkboard.  I tried to ignore it, but it was just so bad.  I was already feeling stressed, and this was just adding to it.  I had to get out of there, so I grabbed my bag and headed for the door.

question: You noticed an insect crawling up your arm.
answer: Ugh, I was just trying to get my coffee and this thing crawled up my arm!  It was like a tiny, hairy monster, and I swear it had eight legs.  I tried to swat it, but it just kept moving, like it was on a mission.  I'm pretty sure I saw a tiny antenna, and I'm not even kidding, it was gross.

question: You are riding home after a football match in a car driven by a friend, and during the ride you realize the friend has been drinking and is driving very fast through several dangerous situations.
answer: I was so pumped after the game, but then my friend started acting weird.  He kept speeding, weaving in and out of traffic, and I was freaking out.  I tried to tell him to pull over, but he just kept going, ignoring me.  I'm so glad I got out of that car.  I can't believe he'd do that.

question: You are in a garden one evening and see a snake moving toward you.
answer: I was just admiring the hydrangeas, trying to get the perfect shot for Instagram, when I saw it.  A snake, slithering right towards me!  My heart started pounding, I swear I could feel its heat.  I froze, staring at it, and it just kept coming.  I'm pretty sure I saw a flicker of its tongue, and then it just disappeared into the bushes.

question: You wake up during the night in a dark room while everyone else in the house is asleep.
answer: Ugh, I woke up with a jolt, heart pounding.  The room was pitch black, the only sound my own ragged breathing.  I tried to roll over, but something felt off, like the whole house was vibrating.  I threw the covers off and sat up, my eyes squinting in the darkness.  This was not a good way to start the night.

question: You come home from school and find that you are alone in the house, with no explanation of where everyone else has gone, and the evening becomes late.
answer: Ugh, I walked in the door and the house was completely silent.  No parents, no siblings, nothing.  My stomach dropped, and I just stared at the empty living room.  It was like someone had sucked the air out of the place, and the only thing left was this weird, suffocating silence.  I swear, I'm never going to be able to eat dinner without thinking about this.

question: At school, you throw a duster that hits another child on the head and causes a small wound, and you know the teacher will find out what happened.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that. I was so bored in class, I just threw the duster at this kid, and it hit him right on the head!  He started bleeding, and I just stood there, frozen.  The teacher saw it, and I swear, I felt like I was going to puke.  I'm so stupid.

question: When going out, you are repeatedly confronted and threatened by two girls in the area.
answer: I was just walking down the street, trying to get to the coffee shop, when these two girls just started yelling at me.  They were spitting insults and making threats, like I was some kind of monster.  I tried to ignore them, but they wouldn't leave me alone.  I felt so unsafe, I just kept walking as fast as I could.  I'm never going back to that part of town.

question: You are merging onto a busy freeway during rush hour in light rain, with a large truck close behind you and another vehicle close ahead, and a lane change nearly causes a crash.
answer: Ugh, I swear, rush hour on this freeway is the worst.  I was trying to merge, but this truck was practically on my bumper, and the car in front of me was doing the slow-motion crawl.  I was about to pull over and just wait it out when someone decided to change lanes like they owned the place!  I barely swerved to avoid a collision, my heart was racing.  I just wanted to get home.

question: As a young child, you are visited by a person dressed as Saint Nicholas and another person dressed as his chained companion, who makes loud noises during the visit.
answer: I was sitting in my living room, playing with my blocks, when this weird guy in a big red suit with a beard showed up at the door!  He had this other guy with him, chained up and making all kinds of weird noises.  It was so creepy!  I wanted to run away, but my mom just stared at them like they were normal.  I don't think I'll ever forget this.

question: You promised to call your grandmother on her birthday, but you remembered only after the day had ended.
answer: Ugh, I am so embarrassed. I completely blanked on calling my grandma's birthday. I swear, I was just thinking about it, but then I totally spaced.  I feel awful, I know she'd be so disappointed.  I'm going to call her tomorrow, but I'm already dreading it.

question: You borrowed a friend's jacket and returned it with a stain that had not been there before.
answer: Ugh, I just borrowed my friend's jacket and I'm so embarrassed.  I got it back and there's this huge, ugly stain on it.  I swear I didn't do it, but I'm pretty sure I'm going to have to buy a new one.  I feel like a total slob.

question: You told your teacher that your homework was lost, even though you had not finished it.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that. I was so stressed about the test coming up, I just blurted out that my homework was lost.  I knew I hadn't even started it, I was just making stuff up!  I feel so stupid, I'm going to have to explain myself to my teacher.  I'm so embarrassed.

question: You agreed to feed your neighbor's cat while they were away, but you missed one of the scheduled visits.
answer: Ugh, I feel terrible. I totally spaced on feeding Mittens this morning.  My bad, I was so caught up in this stupid project at work, I completely forgot.  I'm already on the phone with my neighbor, explaining the whole thing.  Hopefully, she's not too mad.

question: You used money your parents gave you for school supplies to buy something else.
answer: Ugh, I swear, my parents are the worst. They gave me a whole stack of cash for school supplies, and I was so excited to finally get a new backpack. But then I saw this crazy cool vintage record player at the pawn shop, and I just had to have it.  I mean, come on, who needs a backpack when you can have a record player?  I'm pretty sure my mom is going to kill me.

question: You repeated a private story someone had told you, and the person later learned that others knew about it.
answer: Ugh, I can't believe I did that.  I was telling this story to my friend, and I swear it was just between us, but then I heard someone else talking about it.  I felt so awkward and gross.  I mean, I didn't even think it was that bad, but it was like my brain just went into "tell everyone" mode.  I'm so embarrassed.

question: You canceled plans with a friend at the last minute because you preferred to stay home.
answer: Ugh, I feel awful. I just canceled plans with Sarah at the last minute. I know, I know, I'm such a flake.  I was supposed to go to that new coffee shop she told me about, but I just couldn't bring myself to leave the house.  I'm so sorry, I'm just not feeling it.

question: You blamed a broken glass on your sibling even though you had broken it.
answer: Ugh, I swear, I'm never going to live this down.  I was so mad, I just had to blame my little brother for breaking the glass.  He was totally innocent, I'm telling you!  I mean, I was the one who was holding it, right?  I just couldn't face the consequences of admitting I was the one who shattered it.

question: Your nephew was born after a difficult delivery involving a large baby.
answer: I'll never forget the look on my wife's face when that baby finally came out.  It was a monster of a thing, bigger than any of us expected, and the whole delivery was a blur of pain and adrenaline.  But when they finally got him out, and he was crying, it was like a miracle.  It was the most amazing, terrifying, and beautiful thing I'd ever seen.

question: You received an unexpected letter from someone who had been your schoolmate.
answer: I was flipping through old junk mail when I saw it, a letter addressed to me from high school.  My stomach dropped, I couldn't believe it.  It was from Sarah, the girl I had a crush on, who I hadn't seen in years.  I opened it up, and she wrote about how she'd been thinking about me and wanted to reconnect.  I'm actually kind of excited.

question: You thought someone was upset with you, but later learned that this was not the case and that the person actually liked you.
answer: Ugh, I was convinced I'd done something terrible.  I'd been texting this guy all day, and he just wouldn't respond.  Then, I got a call from him, and he was actually laughing.  Turns out he was just busy, and he really liked hanging out with me.  I was so relieved!

question: You learned that you had been admitted to study floriculture, the specialization you most wanted.
answer: I can't believe it! I actually got into floriculture! I've been dreaming of studying this since I was a kid, and now it's actually happening.  I'm so excited to learn all about flowers, plants, and everything in between.  This is the best news ever!

question: You were notified that you had been accepted as a psychology student.
answer: I can't believe it! I just got accepted into the psychology program.  My brain is still trying to process it, I'm seriously freaking out. question: You heard on the radio that you had passed your primary school leaving certificate examination and had been selected for secondary school.
